name: AIGRCeler starter catalog
note: Starter set. The company adopts it as its own and AI Governance owns every change after adoption. Legal mappings are indicative pointers, not legal advice.

controls.title: Name the AI Governance lead and a deputy
controls.objective: Someone with authority is accountable for how AI is governed here.
controls.requirement: Appoint a lead and a deputy for AI Governance, and record the appointment and what they may decide.
acceptance: A signed note or charter names the lead and deputy
It states what they may approve and accept

controls.title: Adopt a short AI principles statement
controls.objective: Everyone knows what the company will and will not do with AI.
controls.requirement: Leadership adopts a one-page statement of AI principles (fairness, safety, privacy, transparency, accountability) and shares it.
acceptance: The statement is dated and approved by leadership
It says how it relates to the company's security, privacy and ethics policies
Staff using AI can find it

controls.title: Register the AI system in the company AI inventory
controls.objective: The company knows every AI system it runs, what it is for and who owns it.
controls.requirement: Record the system's name, purpose, owner, users, data used, vendor and where it runs in the AI inventory.
acceptance: The entry exists and is complete
It matches how the system is really used
evidence_types: screenshot or export of the inventory entry

controls.title: Name a business owner for the system's outcomes
controls.objective: One person answers for what the system does to customers and the business.
controls.requirement: Name a business owner who accepts responsibility for the system's results and for acting on problems.
acceptance: The business owner is named in writing
They have confirmed they accept the role

controls.title: Set a simple acceptable-use rule for staff
controls.objective: Staff know what they may and may not do with AI tools.
controls.requirement: Publish a short rule: approved tools, what data may be entered, what needs a human check, and who to ask.
acceptance: The rule is published and dated
Staff have been told about it
Staff know how to raise a concern about AI use
evidence_types: proof it was shared (email, intranet post)

controls.title: Give people who use or oversee the system basic AI training
controls.objective: People using the system understand what it can and cannot do.
controls.requirement: Train everyone who uses, reviews or oversees the system on its purpose, limits and how to report problems; repeat each year.
acceptance: The people involved are listed as trained within the last year

controls.title: Agree how risks are accepted and exceptions are recorded
controls.objective: Risks are accepted by the right people, in writing.
controls.requirement: Document who may accept which level of residual risk, how exceptions are requested, and how long they last.
acceptance: The rule names roles for each risk level
It says how exceptions are recorded and when they end
evidence_types: the written rule or charter section

controls.title: Write down the intended purpose and check it is not a prohibited use
controls.objective: The system is only used for what it was designed for, and never for banned uses.
controls.requirement: State the intended purpose, users and limits, and confirm in writing that the use is not one the law prohibits.
acceptance: A named person has checked the list of prohibited uses

controls.title: Record how the system is classified under the EU AI Act
controls.objective: The company knows which legal duties apply and why.
controls.requirement: Classify the system (prohibited, high-risk, transparency duty, minimal risk) and record the reasoning and date.
acceptance: The classification and reasoning are written

controls.title: Complete the legal steps required before a high-risk system goes live
controls.objective: A high-risk system is not placed on the market without its required checks.
controls.requirement: Complete and record the conformity assessment, declaration and registration that apply to the system.
acceptance: The required assessment route is identified
Declaration and registration are complete or scheduled before launch

controls.title: Assess the impact on people's fundamental rights
controls.objective: The company has thought through how the system could affect people's rights before launch.
controls.requirement: Carry out and record an assessment of the groups affected, the rights at stake, the likelihood and severity of harm, and the measures taken.
acceptance: The affected groups and rights are named
Harms are rated and each has a measure

controls.title: List the obligations specific to your sector
controls.objective: Rules that apply because of the industry are not missed.
controls.requirement: List the sector rules that touch this system (for example banking, health or insurance supervision) and show how each is met.
acceptance: Each has a named owner and a status

controls.title: Review the AI system and its controls every year
controls.objective: The system and its controls still fit how it is really used.
controls.requirement: Once a year, review purpose, data, performance, incidents and controls, and record what changed.
acceptance: Decisions from the review are listed

controls.title: Agree what changes need approval again
controls.objective: Important changes do not slip in unreviewed.
controls.requirement: Define which changes (purpose, data, model, vendor, users, new countries) must go back to AI Governance, and how they are submitted.
acceptance: The list of triggers is written
Engineering and operations know the route

controls.title: Talk with the people the system affects
controls.objective: The people affected have a say in how the system is built and used.
controls.requirement: Identify affected groups (for a workplace system, the workers and their representatives), ask for their views before launch and at least yearly, and record what changed because of it.
acceptance: Their feedback and the response are recorded

controls.title: Keep a company-level AI risk register
controls.objective: Risks that belong to the company, not one system, are visible.
controls.requirement: Track company-level risks (AI skills, readiness, unclear accountability, complexity) with owners and review them twice a year.
acceptance: It was reviewed in the last six months

controls.title: Assess the impact of the AI system on individuals, groups and society
controls.objective: The company has weighed who the system helps and who it could harm, before launch and whenever its use changes.
controls.requirement: Write a short impact assessment: who is affected (including vulnerable groups), the benefits, the possible harms with their likelihood and severity, effects on society and the environment, the alternatives considered (including doing without AI), and the measures taken. Repeat it when the use changes and at each yearly review.
acceptance: Affected groups, including vulnerable ones, are named
Benefits, harms, likelihood and severity are written down
Alternatives, including no AI, were considered
The business owner and AI Governance have signed it off

playbook.howto: Start from the answers in the discovery record (who is affected, worst case, vulnerable groups). Keep it to two pages.

controls.title: Carry out your duties as provider, importer, distributor or authorised representative under the EU AI Act
controls.objective: When the company puts a high-risk AI system on the EU market, it does what the law asks of its role.
controls.requirement: Confirm the company's role with counsel and, for that role, record how each duty is met: technical documentation, conformity assessment and CE marking, registration, corrective actions and informing authorities, cooperation with authorities, and the appointed representative where the provider is outside the EU.
acceptance: Counsel has confirmed the company's role in writing
Each duty of that role has an owner and a status
A representative is appointed where one is required

controls.title: Retire or replace the AI system safely
controls.objective: When the system is switched off or replaced, people, data and records are handled properly.
controls.requirement: Agree when and how the system will be retired or replaced: who decides, how users and affected people are told, what happens to the data and the model, which records are kept and for how long, and what takes over its work.
acceptance: A retirement or replacement plan exists
Data deletion and record keeping are decided
Users and the systems that depend on it know the plan

controls.title: Know your data: sources, owners and purpose
controls.objective: Every dataset the system uses is known, owned and used for a stated reason.
controls.requirement: List each dataset (source, owner, purpose, personal-data content, where kept) and keep the list current.
acceptance: Every dataset is listed with an owner

tools: data catalog tools such as OpenMetadata or DataHub

controls.title: Have a lawful basis and give notice when using personal data
controls.objective: Personal data is used only with a valid reason and people are told.
controls.requirement: Identify the legal basis for each use of personal data and show the notice given to the people concerned.
acceptance: A lawful basis is recorded for each use
The notice text exists and has been published

controls.title: Honour withdrawal of consent and opt-outs all the way through
controls.objective: When someone withdraws consent or opts out, it takes effect everywhere the data went.
controls.requirement: Provide a way to withdraw or opt out, and show that requests reach the training data, stored data and the vendors.
acceptance: A test request was traced end to end

controls.title: Carry out a data protection impact assessment where it is required
controls.objective: High-risk uses of personal data are assessed before they start.
controls.requirement: Run and record a data protection impact assessment, including measures to reduce each high risk.
acceptance: Remaining high risks are accepted by the right person

controls.title: Check where training and reference data comes from
controls.objective: Data is trusted only after its source and integrity are checked.
controls.requirement: Validate each source (who supplied it, how, under what terms) and keep a chain of custody from source to use.
acceptance: A change history exists for each dataset

playbook.howto: Record where each dataset came from, who approved it, and a fingerprint (hash) of each version.

controls.title: Check data quality before and during use
controls.objective: Bad data is caught before it harms results.
controls.requirement: Run automated checks (completeness, ranges, duplicates, freshness) on data that feeds the system, document how the data is cleaned and labelled, and act on failures.
acceptance: Failures raise an alert and are followed up

controls.title: Check that data represents the people affected
controls.objective: Training and test data reflects the people the system will meet.
controls.requirement: Compare the make-up of training and test data to the people affected; record gaps and what was done about them.
acceptance: Gaps and responses are written down

controls.title: Protect data with access control and encryption
controls.objective: Only the right people can reach the data, and it is protected in storage and on the move.
controls.requirement: Limit access to the data to named roles, encrypt it in storage and transit, and review who has access.
acceptance: Encryption is on for storage and transfer

controls.title: Protect training and reference data from tampering
controls.objective: Nobody can quietly alter the data the model learns from or looks up.
controls.requirement: Use integrity checks, restricted write access and review of unusual changes on training and reference data.
acceptance: Write access is limited and logged
Integrity checks run and failures are followed up

controls.title: Keep personal and confidential data out of prompts and logs
controls.objective: Sensitive information does not end up where it should not be.
controls.requirement: Block or mask personal and confidential data before it reaches the model, prompts or logs, and check the rule works.
acceptance: Masking or blocking is in place
A test with sample sensitive data was blocked or masked

controls.title: Set how long data is kept and how it is deleted
controls.objective: Data is not kept longer than needed and can be erased.
controls.requirement: Define retention periods for training data, prompts, outputs and logs, and show deletion works.

controls.title: Know what data leaves the company when you use a vendor
controls.objective: Company data is not shared with a vendor by accident.
controls.requirement: Document what data is sent to each vendor, what the vendor may do with it, and confirm the settings (for example no training on your data).
acceptance: Data flows to the vendor are listed
Vendor use of your data is limited in writing

controls.title: Collect and keep only the data you need
controls.objective: The system uses the least personal data that does the job.
controls.requirement: Review each personal-data field and remove those not needed; record the decision.
acceptance: Unneeded fields were removed or justified

controls.title: Extra safeguards for sensitive personal data
controls.objective: Sensitive data (health, beliefs, biometrics and similar) gets stronger protection.
controls.requirement: Apply and record a specific legal ground, tighter access and stronger review for sensitive data.
acceptance: Access is limited to named people

controls.title: Keep a record of the data behind every trained version
controls.objective: You can show which data produced which version of the model.
controls.requirement: For every trained version record the datasets, filters and splits used.
acceptance: Each version links to its data

controls.title: Test whether the model can reveal its training data
controls.objective: The model does not give away the data it learned from.
controls.requirement: Run extraction and membership tests against the model and record what was found and fixed.
acceptance: Tests were run on the current version

controls.title: Document the model: design, training approach and limits
controls.objective: Anyone reviewing the model can see how it was built and where it should not be used.
controls.requirement: Write a model description covering purpose, design, training data and method, performance and known limits.
acceptance: The description is complete and dated

controls.title: Set accuracy targets and test against them before release
controls.objective: The system is only released when it meets agreed performance targets.
controls.requirement: Agree measurable targets (accuracy, error rates) with the business, test the system against them on realistic data, and keep the results.
acceptance: Results on realistic data meet them
The model version tested is stated

controls.title: Test unusual and extreme inputs
controls.objective: The system behaves safely when it meets something unexpected.
controls.requirement: Test boundary conditions, rare cases and bad inputs, and record how the system behaves and what was fixed.
acceptance: Failures were fixed or accepted with a reason

controls.title: Test the results for fairness across groups
controls.objective: The system does not treat groups of people unfairly.
controls.requirement: Measure results for each relevant group, compare them against an agreed tolerance, and record fixes.
acceptance: Gaps are within tolerance or explained and accepted

playbook.howto: Choose the groups and the measure with Legal. Compare approval or error rates between groups and record the gap.

controls.title: Make results explainable enough for the use
controls.objective: People affected, and those who oversee the system, can understand why it produced a result.
controls.requirement: Provide explanations suited to the audience (reviewers, affected people) and test that they are understandable.
acceptance: Explanations exist for reviewers and for affected people
A sample was checked for being understandable

controls.title: Test resistance to deliberately misleading inputs
controls.objective: Attackers cannot easily fool the model.
controls.requirement: Run adversarial tests suited to the model type and record findings and fixes.
acceptance: Tests ran on the current version

controls.title: Red-team the AI system
controls.objective: Skilled people try to break or misuse the system before real attackers do.
controls.requirement: Run a structured red-team exercise (jailbreaks, misuse, data extraction, harmful actions) on the system as deployed, and fix what is found.
acceptance: Scope and attack types are written
High findings were fixed or accepted by the right person

playbook.howto: Test the real deployed system, not only the model. Cover prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, harmful content and misuse of any tools the system can call.

controls.title: Check the AI software code and libraries for weaknesses
controls.objective: The code and components are free of known security flaws.
controls.requirement: Scan the AI application's code and dependencies for vulnerabilities, fix serious findings and repeat on each release.

playbook.howto: Run the scanner in your build pipeline and send the SARIF or JSON result.

controls.title: Test the running system and its connections for weaknesses
controls.objective: Live interfaces, APIs and plug-ins resist attack.
controls.requirement: Test the running application, its APIs and any plug-ins with dynamic security testing and fix serious findings.
acceptance: The live system and APIs were tested

controls.title: Test prompt injection and jailbreaks
controls.objective: Instructions hidden in inputs cannot take over the system.
controls.requirement: Test the system with known prompt-injection and jailbreak patterns, including indirect injection through documents and web content.
acceptance: Failures led to fixes or limits

controls.title: Filter harmful, wrong or confidential output
controls.objective: Harmful or confidential content is stopped before it reaches a person.
controls.requirement: Put output checks in place (harmful content, confidential data, unsupported claims) and test that they work.
acceptance: A test showed they block known bad cases

controls.title: Control versions and approve each release
controls.objective: Only reviewed versions of the model, prompt and settings reach users.
controls.requirement: Keep the model, prompts and settings under version control and require a recorded approval for each release.
evidence_types: release log or screenshot of the process

controls.title: Re-test after any change
controls.objective: A change cannot silently make the system worse.
controls.requirement: After any change to model, data, prompts or settings, re-run the key tests and compare with the last accepted results.
acceptance: Comparison with the previous version is kept

controls.title: Make training reproducible
controls.objective: A past model version can be rebuilt and checked.
controls.requirement: Record code, data versions, settings and random seeds for each trained version.

controls.title: Protect the model itself
controls.objective: The model cannot easily be copied or extracted.
controls.requirement: Restrict access to model files, limit and monitor query volumes, and alert on extraction-like behaviour.
acceptance: Rate limits and monitoring are active

controls.title: Test that generated answers stay grounded in facts
controls.objective: Generated answers are checked against trusted sources.
controls.requirement: Measure how often answers are unsupported or invented using a test set, and keep the result above an agreed level.
acceptance: A test set and target exist

controls.title: Check the vendor before you rely on it
controls.objective: You know who you are depending on and what they do with AI.
controls.requirement: Do and record due diligence on the vendor: who they are, security practices, AI practices, where data is held.

controls.title: Get the right terms in the vendor contract
controls.objective: The contract covers data use, audit, incident notice and liability.
controls.requirement: Make sure the contract covers data use limits, security, incident notice time, audit rights, sub-suppliers and liability.
acceptance: Each topic is covered or a gap is accepted in writing

controls.title: Obtain the vendor's documentation and stated limits
controls.objective: You know what the vendor says the system can and cannot do.
controls.requirement: Obtain and file the vendor's model documentation, intended use, known limits and update policy.
acceptance: Stated limits are compared with your use

controls.title: Agree how the vendor tells you about changes
controls.objective: You hear about model or version changes before your users feel them.
controls.requirement: Agree a change-notice route and notice period, and check that notices reach the right person.
acceptance: The route and period are written
A recent notice reached the right person

controls.title: Test the vendor's system on your own cases
controls.objective: The vendor's claims hold for your data and users.
controls.requirement: Test the vendor's system on a realistic sample of your own cases, including fairness and unusual inputs, before relying on it.

controls.title: Keep the vendor's security assurance current
controls.objective: The vendor's security claims are independently supported.
controls.requirement: Obtain the vendor's current security attestation (for example SOC 2 or ISO 27001) and review exceptions.

controls.title: Have a plan for leaving or replacing the vendor
controls.objective: A vendor failure or exit does not stop the business.
controls.requirement: Write and keep a plan for switching or stopping the system, including data return.

controls.title: Check licences and open-source obligations
controls.objective: Model and software licences allow your use.
controls.requirement: List the licences of models, data and software and confirm your use complies.

controls.title: Check downloaded models and components are genuine and safe
controls.objective: Third-party models and libraries have not been tampered with.
controls.requirement: Verify source and fingerprints of downloaded models and libraries, scan them, and keep a bill of materials.

controls.title: Review where the vendor and its sub-suppliers hold your data
controls.objective: You know which companies and countries handle your data.
controls.requirement: List the vendor's sub-suppliers and data locations and confirm transfers are lawful.

controls.title: Write down who is responsible for what between you and the vendor
controls.objective: It is clear which duties sit with the vendor and which with you.
controls.requirement: Record the split of responsibilities (provider, deployer, other parties) for each legal and operating duty.

controls.title: Record what the base model and your fine-tuning data bring
controls.objective: Limits and risks inherited from a base model are known.
controls.requirement: Document the base model, its known limits and the data used to adapt it.
acceptance: Base model and tuning data are documented

controls.title: Know how to reach the vendor in an incident and how fast they respond
controls.objective: When something goes wrong, the vendor can be reached and acts fast.
controls.requirement: Record vendor incident contacts and response times and test the route once a year.

controls.title: Get the documentation and terms from the provider of the general-purpose AI model you rely on
controls.objective: You know what the model provider has told you about its model, how it was trained and what it cannot do.
controls.requirement: Obtain from the model provider the information it must make available to those who build on its model (what it can do, its limits, a summary of how it was trained, how to use it safely) and its policy on copyright and data use, and compare it with your use.
acceptance: The provider's documentation is on file
Its stated limits were compared with your use
Its policy on data and copyright was read

controls.title: Watch accuracy and drift in live use
controls.objective: Loss of quality is noticed early.
controls.requirement: Track key quality measures in production, set tolerances, and alert when they are crossed.

controls.title: Watch fairness in live use
controls.objective: Unfair patterns that appear in real use are noticed.
controls.requirement: Track the fairness measure chosen in testing on live results and alert on drift.

controls.title: Watch for attacks and strange inputs
controls.objective: Attacks and abuse show up quickly.
controls.requirement: Monitor for unusual input patterns, spikes and policy-violating use, with alerts to Security.

controls.title: Give people only the access they need, and review it
controls.objective: Access to the system, data and settings is limited and reviewed.
controls.requirement: Use role-based, least-privilege access to the AI system, its data and its settings, and review the list at least twice a year.
acceptance: The list was reviewed in the last six months

controls.title: Keep secrets and API keys safe
controls.objective: Keys and passwords cannot leak or be misused.
controls.requirement: Store keys in a secret manager, rotate them, and keep them out of code and prompts.

controls.title: Keep logs that let you trace what the system did
controls.objective: Decisions can be reconstructed afterwards.
controls.requirement: Log inputs, outputs, versions and human actions in a protected store for the required period.
acceptance: Logs cover inputs, outputs and versions

controls.title: Have an incident plan that covers AI failures
controls.objective: Problems are handled fast and by the right people.
controls.requirement: Write an incident plan with a severity scale, who is told and how fast, regulator notice duties and a named contact.
acceptance: Severity scale and response times are written

controls.title: Practise the incident plan
controls.objective: The team can act under pressure.
controls.requirement: Run a table-top exercise on an AI incident each year and record lessons.
acceptance: An exercise was held in the last year

controls.title: Be able to stop or isolate the system quickly (circuit breaker)
controls.objective: A runaway system can be stopped before it does lasting harm.
controls.requirement: Provide a tested way to stop or isolate the system or its actions quickly, and name who may use it.

controls.title: Map what depends on the system and what could cascade
controls.objective: A failure here does not take down other things unnoticed.
controls.requirement: Map downstream systems and processes and analyze how a failure would spread.

controls.title: Protect the build and deployment pipeline
controls.objective: Nobody can alter what is released without being noticed.
controls.requirement: Control and log access to build, training and deployment pipelines and sign what is released.

controls.title: Do not go live without AI Governance sign-off
controls.objective: The system cannot go live until its required controls are approved and verified.
controls.requirement: Make go-live depend on the launch-status file or an equivalent recorded sign-off, and show the step in your release process.
acceptance: The release process checks the sign-off
A release was blocked or passed on that basis

playbook.howto: The tool publishes a small status file for each AI system. Your engineers can have the release pipeline read it.

controls.title: Be able to roll back and recover
controls.objective: A bad change can be undone fast.
controls.requirement: Keep a tested rollback and recovery plan for the model, prompts and data.

controls.title: Limit what an AI agent can do on its own
controls.objective: An agent cannot cause serious harm through its tools.
controls.requirement: Allow only listed tools and actions, cap spending and volume, and require a person's approval for irreversible or high-impact actions.
acceptance: Approval is required for high-impact actions
A test confirmed the limits hold

controls.title: Watch explainability signals in live use
controls.objective: Explanations stay understandable and trustworthy in real use.
controls.requirement: Sample live explanations, check they are consistent, and review user feedback on them.

controls.title: Review alert thresholds and how alerts are handled
controls.objective: Monitoring stays useful, with neither silence nor noise.
controls.requirement: Review thresholds and alert handling at least twice a year and record changes.

controls.title: Define human oversight: who reviews, when, with what power
controls.objective: A person can understand, question, override or stop the system where it matters.
controls.requirement: Define where a human checks or can override the system, who they are, what they can do, and when they must.
acceptance: Named reviewers have authority to override

controls.title: Train and equip the reviewers
controls.objective: Reviewers can do the job well and have the time to do it.
controls.requirement: Make sure reviewers are trained on the system's limits, have the information they need and are not pushed to approve quickly.

controls.title: Design the screen and process to avoid over-reliance
controls.objective: People keep checking instead of blindly trusting the AI.
controls.requirement: Show uncertainty, require a check for important results, and review whether people just accept everything.

controls.title: Tell people when they are dealing with AI, and label AI content
controls.objective: People know when AI is involved.
controls.requirement: Tell users clearly that they are dealing with AI and mark AI-generated content where required.
acceptance: Notice is shown at first contact
evidence_types: screenshots of the notice and label

controls.title: Explain in plain words what the system does and its limits
controls.objective: Users understand what to expect and not to expect.
controls.requirement: Provide user-facing text on purpose, limits, data use and how to get help.
acceptance: It was checked with real users or staff

controls.title: Give people an explanation and a human review of decisions about them
controls.objective: People can find out why a decision was made and ask for a person to look again.
controls.requirement: Offer an explanation and a human review of any decision with legal or similar effect on a person.
acceptance: The right is described to people
A review route works within a stated time

controls.title: Provide a way to appeal and contest
controls.objective: A person who disagrees with an outcome can challenge it.
controls.requirement: Provide an appeal route with owner, response time and a record of outcomes.
acceptance: The route is described to people

controls.title: Offer a way to report problems
controls.objective: Users and staff can report problems easily and get an answer.
controls.requirement: Give a clear, simple channel to report problems with the system and make sure someone responds.

controls.title: Assess the safety impact before use
controls.objective: Risks to physical or psychological safety are identified and reduced.
controls.requirement: Assess how the system could harm safety, and set measures and limits for each.
acceptance: Each has a measure or limit

controls.title: Check the system is usable and fair for people with different needs
controls.objective: People are not excluded by how the system is built.
controls.requirement: Check accessibility and fair access (language, disability, devices) and record gaps.

controls.title: Learn from appeals and complaints
controls.objective: Patterns in complaints are noticed and acted on.
controls.requirement: Review appeals and complaints each quarter for patterns, and record actions.

controls.title: Offer a human alternative where required
controls.objective: People who prefer or need a human can reach one.
controls.requirement: Provide a route to a human instead of the AI where the law or fairness calls for it.

controls.title: Set a misuse policy and a way to report abuse
controls.objective: Users know what is not allowed and abuse can be reported.
controls.requirement: Publish what users must not do and let people report abuse; act on reports.

controls.title: Check the decision journal is intact
controls.objective: The record of decisions has not been altered.
controls.requirement: Every quarter, run the journal integrity check and send the result.
acceptance: The check passed or breaks were explained

playbook.howto: Ask AIGRCeler to run the journal check and send you the result.

controls.title: Keep evidence for the required period
controls.objective: Evidence is kept as long as the law and your rules require.
controls.requirement: Apply and document the retention period (10 years full lane, 7 standard, 5 light by default) and where evidence is stored.
acceptance: The period is written and applied
Storage is protected and backed up

controls.title: Assemble the technical documentation pack
controls.objective: A regulator or auditor can see how the system was built and governed.
controls.requirement: Assemble the technical documentation (design, data, testing, risk management, oversight, changes) in one place.

controls.title: Keep automatic records of system use
controls.objective: Use can be reconstructed afterwards.
controls.requirement: Keep automatic records of events for the required period and protect them.
acceptance: Records are kept for the period

controls.title: Audit the AI governance program yearly
controls.objective: Someone checks that the program does what it says.
controls.requirement: Once a year, audit a sample of controls, evidence and decisions, and report findings to leadership.

controls.title: Be ready to answer a regulator
controls.objective: Questions from a regulator get a fast, complete answer.
controls.requirement: Name who deals with regulators, where evidence is, and how quickly you can produce it.
acceptance: A trial request was answered in the stated time

controls.title: Plan monitoring after the system is on the market
controls.objective: Real-world performance is tracked for the life of the system.
controls.requirement: Write a post-market monitoring plan with what is measured, how often and who reviews it.
acceptance: It matches the controls in place

controls.title: Be ready to report serious incidents to authorities
controls.objective: Serious incidents reach the authority in time.
controls.requirement: Prepare contacts, templates and timelines for reporting serious incidents.

controls.title: Give deployers and users the information they need
controls.objective: Those who rely on your system get the documentation required.
controls.requirement: Provide instructions for use, limits and contact details to users and deployers.

controls.title: Write a short lessons-learned note after each incident and each yearly review
controls.objective: The program learns and gets better.
controls.requirement: After each incident and each annual review, record what was learned and what changes in controls.
acceptance: A note exists for each event
Changes are traced to the catalog
